analysis:
Two changes were examined. (1) docs/reference/configuration.md head lines 553-555 add DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. This is documentation only, but it describes runtime behavior. Paged KV pools keep up to min(2 GiB, grant/8) of free segments uncommitted and uncharged, and reinstall them at admission. They are dropped on memory pressure, before load gates and after 30 s idle. New whole-page segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages without a stream fence. (2) EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift head line 458 passes `environment: environment` to makeSegmentedPagedBackend, so the segment-retention env flags are read from the caller-supplied environment map rather than the process environment. The environment parameter defaults to ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment and is already used for the KV policy, so no new trust input appears. The callee, EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, was not supplied, so I cannot verify the retention logic.

Relevant threats: T-028 (residual KV/GPU data across requests), T-010 and T-029 (availability and memory), and T-041 (prefix cache, unaffected here). Retained segments are never exposed to a different consumer through reads of unwritten positions in the visible evidence, and they stay inside the same attested provider process. T-028 already accepts residual in-process data, so I found no concrete regression.

Open questions for deeper review of the unsupplied callee:
- Do reinstalled retained segments have stale-content semantics, such as an attention-mask or valid-length guarantee, so prior-request KV can never be read?
- Is retention cleared on model unload and on the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE or purge paths?
- Is the uncharged retained memory (up to 2 GiB) correctly counted as reclaimable by the admission and load gates, to avoid a memory-DoS?
- Is the host zero-fill path correct on alignment, so no uninitialized pages are wrapped?
